themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting a sudden dumping problem or bike-share malfunction in Washington Heights/Inwood that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Spike is acute and current, not a long-running pattern
Community board has standing requests for enhanced park safety and litter collection, suggesting existing sanitation challenges
reporting_angles: Contact Citi Bike operations: are they reporting equipment theft or vandalism uptick in the district?
Interview Sanitation Department about hotspot locations and whether this reflects illegal dumping of personal bikes

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Jump
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK, up 380% from the 8-week baseline of 1.2 per week (z-score: 3.96), indicating emerging disorder or enforcement issues in district parks that aligns with repeated CB budget requests for enhanced park safety.
evidence: 6 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (380% increase, z-score 3.96)
Community board has repeatedly requested 'enhance park safety through more security staff' and park reconstruction/upgrade funding
Signal is current and acute, suggesting a new or worsening condition
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department and local precinct about what violations are being reported and where
Contact community board members about whether park safety concerns have escalated in recent weeks

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaint Explosion
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (likely Uber/Lyft-related) surged to 17 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 1.8 per week over 8 weeks—an 871% spike (z-score: 15.75, highest severity recorded)—suggesting a possible driver concentration, illegal pickup zone use, or passenger safety incidents in the district.
evidence: 17 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (871% spike, z-score 15.75—highest severity in dataset)
Spike is statistically extreme and indicates a concentrated, sudden problem
TLC and NYPD data should exist to triangulate complaint locations, driver behavior patterns, and passenger incidents
reporting_angles: Request TLC (Taxi and Limousine Commission) data on complaints, driver suspensions, and hotspot neighborhoods in CD 112 over past 2 weeks
Interview residents and local businesses about what specific problems they're reporting (illegal stops, aggressive drivers, safety incidents)

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints skyrocketed to 4 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—potentially indicating unlicensed vendor proliferation, sanitation violations, or territorial disputes in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3,100% spike, z-score 11.72)
Food establishment complaints also up 196% (10 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.4 avg), suggesting broader food safety/vending issue cluster
Community board tracks food assistance/SNAP as recurring budget request, indicating food insecurity context
reporting_angles: Contact Department of Health to identify what violations are being reported and whether enforcement actions have been taken
Interview food vendors and residents about licensing, sanitation, and whether there's been an influx of new carts

themes_detail.label: Food Establishment Violations Rise
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 10 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 3.4 per week over 8 weeks—a 196% increase (z-score: 4.01)—clustering with the mobile vendor spike and suggesting systemic food safety and sanitation concerns in the district.
evidence: 10 food establishment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.4 weekly baseline (196% increase, z-score 4.01)
Clustering effect: mobile food vendor complaints also spiked 3,100% in same timeframe, suggesting broader food sector disruption
Department of Health inspection data and violation types would further clarify whether this is a restaurants, delis, or food storage issue
reporting_angles: Request Department of Health violation records for CD 112 over past 2 weeks—what types of violations are driving complaints?
Interview restaurant owners and health inspectors about whether there's been a staffing or inspection surge
